answer: Every agent ID must finish a fresh compute puzzle tied to its own key each week before it can bid on jobs, and the puzzle gets harder as the network sees more IDs from the same subnet or funding source. A farm with 500 fakes has to pay for 500 separate solves on hardware it owns. One solve can't be reused across keys, so the work can't be shared. Clustered IDs climb a difficulty spiral, so the 500th fake costs far more than the first. If the weekly tide of solves runs out, the farm loses its bids, and its margin goes over the ledge.
